Definition: from G3725; to mark out or bound ("horizon"), i.e. (figuratively) to appoint, decree, specify:--declare, determine, limit, ordain.
BiblicalUsage: When Scripture says horízō, it means declare, determine, limit, ordain. The word appears 8 times, and in Luke, Acts, Romans, and Hebrews it carries that same straightforward meaning. Nothing hidden sits behind it; the sense is the one you would expect from the word itself.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that horízō matters because God appoints the times and the boundaries, and nothing happens outside His determination. My position is simple: I take God at His word here, and I build on that.
